questions.question: A tractor-trailer may take up to ____ percent longer to stop in poor weather than in ideal conditions.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles need more distance to stop. In poor weather, a tractor-trailer may take up to 25 percent longer to stop than it would in ideal conditions.

questions.question: When driving near heavy trucks, you must allow for:

options.text: The longer stopping distance required by large vehicles.
The shorter stopping distance required by large vehicles.
The decreased noise of larger vehicles.
The increased speed of larger vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: The longer stopping distance required by large vehicles.
questions.explanation: Heavy trucks need more distance to stop than smaller vehicles. Stay where the truck driver can see you and where you have a clear view of traffic ahead.

questions.question: Vehicle stopping distance does NOT depend on:

options.text: Your reaction time.
The time of day.
Your vehicle's brake condition.
Your vehicle's tire condition and type.

questions.correctAnswerText: The time of day.
questions.explanation: Stopping distance depends on reaction time, weather, visibility, vehicle weight, brake condition, tire condition and type, road conditions, and speed. The time of day does not affect stopping distance.

questions.question: Driving much slower than the speed limit is:

options.text: Illegal.
Smart.
Safe.
Optional.

questions.correctAnswerText: Illegal.
questions.explanation: Driving too slowly blocks traffic and causes unsafe lane changes. It is illegal to drive so slowly that you block the normal flow of traffic.

questions.question: A "Reduced speed, 35 mph" sign means:

options.text: The new 35 mph speed limit starts at this sign.
The new 35 mph speed limit starts at the next speed limit sign.
You have plenty of time to slow down before the reduced speed zone.
You should reduce your speed to 35 mph only in poor weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: The new 35 mph speed limit starts at this sign.
questions.explanation: When you see a "Reduced speed" sign with a new speed limit, that new speed limit begins right at the sign.

questions.question: When you approach a stopped emergency vehicle with flashing lights, you must:

options.text: Slow down and change lanes away from the vehicle if possible.
Drive to the right side of the road and stop.
Stay in your lane and continue at the same speed.
Speed up to quickly pass the stopped vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and change lanes away from the vehicle if possible.
questions.explanation: Always slow down when you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights. Change lanes to give the vehicle extra space if you can do so safely. If you cannot change lanes, slow down and give the vehicle as much room as possible.

questions.question: A bicyclist who breaks traffic laws:

options.text: Is allowed to do so because bicyclists do not have to obey traffic laws.
Can be ticketed.
Will always get a warning from police.
Will have their bicycle taken away.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can be ticketed.
questions.explanation: Bicyclists have the same rights and responsibilities as drivers. Both can be ticketed for breaking traffic laws.

questions.question: When an intersection is blocked by traffic ahead, you should:

options.text: Move slowly until traffic ahead moves.
Get as close as possible to the car in front.
Stay out of the intersection until you can drive all the way through.
Use your horn to make cars move.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay out of the intersection until you can drive all the way through.
questions.explanation: Do not enter an intersection if traffic is blocked on the other side. Wait until traffic clears so you can pass completely through the intersection.

questions.question: The default speed limit in business districts is:

options.text: 70 mph.
55 mph.
40 mph.
25 mph.

questions.correctAnswerText: 25 mph.
questions.explanation: The default speed limit in business districts is 25 mph. Follow posted signs if a different speed limit is shown.

questions.question: A flashing yellow light means:

options.text: Stop and look, then go if there is no traffic.
Stop and wait for a green light.
Speed up to clear the intersection quickly.
Slow down and proceed with caution.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed with caution.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down and proceed carefully through the intersection.

questions.question: If there are two railroad tracks next to each other, what should you do?

options.text: It is always safe to proceed after one train passes.
You must always stop before crossing the tracks.
After one train passes, check the other track for a second train before proceeding.
Honk your horn as you cross the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: After one train passes, check the other track for a second train before proceeding.
questions.explanation: With two railroad tracks side by side, watch for a second train after one passes. Do not cross until you are sure no train is coming on either track.

questions.question: When parking downhill on a two-way street, what should you do?

options.text: Turn your wheels to the right.
Turn your wheels to the left.
Keep your wheels pointed straight ahead.
Leave your transmission in neutral.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your wheels to the right.
questions.explanation: When parking downhill, turn your wheels toward the side of the road. If your car rolls, it will roll away from traffic.

questions.question: What do regulatory signs do?

options.text: Are placed in every location where there is a present danger.
Tell drivers what they must or must not do.
Are diamond-shaped and yellow or green.
May warn drivers that they are approaching a school zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tell drivers what they must or must not do.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs are usually rectangular with black text on white background. They tell drivers what they must or must not do, such as speed limits or no passing rules.

questions.question: Why should drivers be extra alert to motorcyclists, bicyclists, and pedestrians?

options.text: They are hard to see in traffic.
They obey different traffic laws than larger motor vehicles.
They always have the right-of-way.
They don't have rearview mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are hard to see in traffic.
questions.explanation: Many crashes happen because drivers did not see motorcycles, bicycles, or pedestrians. These are smaller and harder to spot than cars. Stay alert to avoid hitting them.

questions.question: When merging onto a freeway, what should you do?

options.text: Proceed slowly while waiting for an opening.
Accelerate to a speed faster than freeway traffic.
Turn on your hazard lights until safely on the freeway.
Accelerate to match freeway traffic speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Accelerate to match freeway traffic speed.
questions.explanation: Use the on-ramp to speed up to match freeway traffic. This lets you merge safely and smoothly. You must yield to traffic already on the freeway.

questions.question: What does a single broken white line down the center of a two-lane road mean?

options.text: Lanes move in opposite directions and passing is not allowed.
Lanes move in opposite directions and passing is allowed when safe.
Lanes move in the same direction and passing is not allowed.
Lanes move in the same direction and passing is allowed when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lanes move in the same direction and passing is allowed when safe.
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic moving the same direction. A broken line means you can pass when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: How much alcohol does your body eliminate in one hour?

options.text: Three alcoholic drinks.
One alcoholic drink.
Two alcoholic drinks.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: One alcoholic drink.
questions.explanation: Your body gets rid of about one drink per hour. How impaired you become depends on how much you drink, how fast, your weight, food intake, and overall health.

questions.question: A red flashing traffic light means the same thing as a:

options.text: Solid red light.
Stop sign.
Yield sign.
Caution sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop sign.
questions.explanation: A red flashing traffic light means the same as a stop sign. Come to a complete stop and then proceed when safe.

questions.question: When driving on slippery roads, what should you do?

options.text: Use alternate routes.
Drive as you would on dry roads.
Increase the distance between you and the car ahead.
Avoid crossing bridges or intersections.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase the distance between you and the car ahead.
questions.explanation: On slippery roads, increase your following distance. Your car may take longer to stop than on dry roads.

questions.question: If a green arrow turns into a solid green light, what can you do?

options.text: You may still turn, but you must yield to oncoming traffic.
You may no longer turn and must go straight.
You still have the right-of-way to turn.
You no longer have to turn in the direction the arrow pointed.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may still turn, but you must yield to oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: When a green arrow becomes a solid green light, you can still turn in that direction. However, you must first let pedestrians and oncoming traffic pass.

questions.question: You must pull over and let an emergency vehicle pass:

options.text: No matter which direction it is coming from.
Only if it is behind you.
Only if it is coming toward you.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: No matter which direction it is coming from.
questions.explanation: Pull over to the right and stop for any emergency vehicle with flashing lights. This applies whether the vehicle is behind you or coming toward you.

questions.question: A broken yellow line down the center of a two-lane road means:

options.text: Traffic moves in opposite directions and you cannot pass.
Traffic moves in opposite directions and you can pass when safe.
Traffic moves in the same direction and you cannot pass.
Traffic moves in the same direction and you can pass when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moves in opposite directions and you can pass when safe.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. A broken line means you can pass when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: When driving on slippery roads:

options.text: Always drive at the speed limit.
Use cruise control to keep a steady speed.
Drive closer to the car ahead.
Do not make sudden changes in speed or direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not make sudden changes in speed or direction.
questions.explanation: Avoid sudden changes in speed or direction on slippery roads. Slow down and do not use cruise control on these surfaces.

questions.question: The Child Passenger Safety Law requires children under age eight and shorter than ____ to use an approved safety seat or booster seat.

options.text: 5 feet, 5 inches
5 feet
4 feet, 11 inches
4 feet, 9 inches

questions.correctAnswerText: 4 feet, 9 inches
questions.explanation: Children under age eight and shorter than 4 feet, 9 inches must be in an approved safety seat or booster seat in the back of the vehicle.

questions.question: A solid white line down the center of a two-lane road means:

options.text: Traffic moves in opposite directions and you cannot pass.
Traffic moves in opposite directions and you can pass when safe.
Traffic moves in the same direction and you cannot pass.
Traffic moves in the same direction and you can pass when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moves in the same direction and you cannot pass.
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. A solid line means you cannot pass.

questions.question: When you approach a railroad crossing with no flashing lights or gates, you should:

options.text: Cross quickly as fast as possible.
Always stop before crossing the tracks.
Be ready to yield to any train at the crossing.
Speed up to cross before a train arrives.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to yield to any train at the crossing.
questions.explanation: Always be ready to yield to trains at railroad crossings, especially when there are no lights or gates. Make sure your entire vehicle can clear the tracks before crossing. Do not shift gears while on the tracks.

questions.question: When entering a highway from an entrance ramp, you should:

options.text: Drive faster than traffic to get ahead.
Enter slowly to avoid other vehicles.
Stop first, then slowly enter traffic.
Speed up to match the traffic speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up to match the traffic speed.
questions.explanation: Use the acceleration lane to speed up to the same speed as traffic. Signal, look for an opening, and merge safely into traffic.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Warns about road conditions ahead or nearby.
Shows you directions to cities and towns.
Tells you traffic laws and rules.
Warns about road construction ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Warns about road conditions ahead or nearby.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with black symbols on a yellow background. They alert you to conditions on or near the road.

questions.question: When you meet an oncoming vehicle on a narrow road, you must:

options.text: Pull completely off the road and stop.
Give the other vehicle at least half of the road.
Tell the other vehicle to pull over.
Turn on your high beams so the other driver sees you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give the other vehicle at least half of the road.
questions.explanation: On narrow roads, allow oncoming vehicles at least half of the road. Both drivers need enough space to pass each other safely.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Slow down if an emergency vehicle is near.
Look both ways before crossing.
Always make a complete stop.
Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.
questions.explanation: Slow down as you approach a yield sign. Be prepared to stop and let other vehicles and pedestrians go first. You must stop if traffic conditions require it.
